title: Statement Close, Interest and the Least Payment Asked on a Northbeam Credit Account
content:
The statement on an account of the Northbeam Store Credit and Financing Accounts range closes on the account's statement day, covering the product's cycle days.

## 1. The least payment the statement asks for

The least payment is the product's percentage of the statement balance raised to the product's money floor, rounded up to the cent. The statement balance is what is owed on the account as the statement closes.

Read as a definition of the resulting amount: take the product's percentage of the statement balance, carried to the cent and rounded up; the least payment is that amount or the product's money floor, whichever of the two is the greater. The percentage never lowers the floor and the floor never lowers the percentage figure.

## 2. Interest

Interest is charged on the balance carried past the product's grace days at the product's purchase rate, worked out on the average daily balance of the statement period. A balance cleared in full inside the grace days is charged nothing.

A promotional financing plan is charged at the product's promotional rate while it runs. On the deferred interest product, a plan not cleared by its end day has the interest accrued from the purchase day become payable in full in that statement period.

## 3. Payments and delivery

A payment is applied as the product's allocation basis states, and the customer may not direct it elsewhere.

The statement is delivered by a way the product offers, and the paper statement fee is charged only where electronic delivery was available and the customer chose paper.

## 4. The least payment worked through, on hypothetical figures

The percentage and money floor used below are hypothetical figures chosen only to work the relationship through; neither is a figure any product in the range sets. Take a product asking a percentage of 2.5 with a money floor of 20.00 US dollars.

| Statement balance | The percentage of it, to the cent, rounded up | The money floor | The greater of the two, being the least payment |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1240.00 | 31.00 | 20.00 | 31.00 |
| 400.00 | 10.00 | 20.00 | 20.00 |
| 1001.37 | 25.04 | 20.00 | 25.04 |

In the first line the percentage governs, because 31.00 stands above the floor. In the second the floor governs, because 10.00 stands below it. The third line shows the rounding: the percentage of 1001.37 comes to 25.03425, which is carried to the cent by rounding up, giving 25.04, and that stands above the floor.

Interest in the same illustration is not worked from any of these figures, since it is charged on the average daily balance of the period rather than on the balance at the close.
